_about: Nerve, arterial and venous supply of muscles and organs for the atlas info card. Keys are model structure names. n / a / v = nerve / artery / vein: t = text shown to the learner, m = model parts to light up (same side as the tapped muscle). Check any change against the lecture notes or a textbook.

a.t: Supratrochlear artery and the supraorbital branches of the ophthalmic artery.

v.t: Supratrochlear and supraorbital veins, draining to the angular vein.

n.t: Masseteric nerve from the anterior division of the mandibular nerve.

v.t: Facial vein and the retromandibular vein.

n.t: Medial pterygoid nerve from the mandibular nerve.

a.t: Maxillary artery.

v.t: Pterygoid venous plexus, which drains to the maxillary vein.

n.t: Mylohyoid nerve, a branch of the inferior alveolar nerve.

n.t: Cardiac plexus: parasympathetic fibres from the vagus nerve and sympathetic cardiac nerves from the upper thoracic ganglia.

a.t: Right and left coronary arteries from the ascending aorta.

v.t: Great, middle and small cardiac veins drain to the coronary sinus.

n.t: Vagus nerve (X): anterior and posterior vagal trunks. Sympathetic fibres reach it through the coeliac plexus.

a.t: Left gastric artery and the short gastric and gastro-omental branches of the splenic artery, all from the coeliac trunk.

v.t: Left gastric veins drain to the portal system, and the gastro-omental veins join the splenic vein.

n.t: Hepatic plexus from the vagus nerve and the sympathetic coeliac plexus.

a.t: Proper hepatic artery, the continuation of the common hepatic artery from the coeliac trunk.

v.t: Hepatic portal vein carries most of the blood from the gut; the hepatic veins drain to the inferior vena cava.

n.t: Vagus nerve (X), and sympathetic fibres from the coeliac and superior mesenteric plexuses.

a.t: Splenic artery and the gastroduodenal and pancreaticoduodenal arteries.

v.t: Splenic vein, which joins the superior mesenteric vein to form the hepatic portal vein.

n.t: Vagus nerve (X) and sympathetic fibres from the coeliac and superior mesenteric plexuses.

a.t: Gastroduodenal and pancreaticoduodenal arteries.

v.t: Veins follow the arteries into the portal system.

n.t: Sympathetic and vagal fibres through the superior mesenteric plexus. The model does not draw these separately.

a.t: Jejunal branches of the superior mesenteric artery.

v.t: Jejunal veins drain to the superior mesenteric vein.

n.t: Vagus nerve (X), with sympathetic fibres from the thoracic sympathetic trunk.

a.t: Oesophageal branches of the thoracic aorta, the left gastric artery and the inferior thyroid artery.

v.t: Oesophageal veins drain to the azygos system and to the left gastric vein.

n.t: Recurrent laryngeal nerves, branches of the vagus nerve (X).

a.t: Inferior thyroid artery.

v.t: Inferior thyroid veins drain to the brachiocephalic veins.

n.t: Recurrent laryngeal and external laryngeal nerves, branches of the vagus nerve (X).

a.t: Superior thyroid artery (from the external carotid) and inferior thyroid artery (from the thyrocervical trunk).

v.t: Superior thyroid vein drains to the internal jugular vein; the inferior thyroid veins drain to the brachiocephalic veins.

n.t: Renal plexus of sympathetic fibres. The model does not draw this separately.

a.t: Renal arteries from the abdominal aorta, each dividing into anterior and posterior branches.

v.t: Renal veins drain to the inferior vena cava.

n.t: Sympathetic splanchnic fibres to the medulla. The model does not draw these separately.

a.t: Superior, middle and inferior suprarenal arteries; the inferior branch comes from the renal artery.

v.t: Suprarenal veins drain to the inferior vena cava on the right and to the left renal vein on the left.

n.t: Vagal and sympathetic fibres through the superior mesenteric plexus.

a.t: Ileocolic and right colic arteries from the superior mesenteric artery.

v.t: Ileocolic and right colic veins drain to the superior mesenteric vein.

n.t: Vagal fibres to the proximal part; sympathetic fibres to the distal part through the mesenteric plexuses.

a.t: Middle colic artery from the superior mesenteric artery, with branches of the left colic artery from the inferior mesenteric artery.

v.t: Middle colic vein drains to the superior mesenteric vein.

n.t: Lumbar splanchnic sympathetic fibres and pelvic splanchnic fibres.

a.t: Left colic artery from the inferior mesenteric artery.
m: Descending branch of left colic artery

v.t: Inferior mesenteric vein.

n.t: Pelvic splanchnic and lumbar sympathetic fibres.

a.t: Sigmoid arteries from the inferior mesenteric artery.

v.t: Sigmoid veins drain to the inferior mesenteric vein.

n.t: Vagal fibres through the superior mesenteric plexus; sympathetic fibres from the coeliac plexus.

a.t: Appendicular artery, a branch of the ileocolic artery.

v.t: Veins drain with the ileocolic vein to the superior mesenteric vein.

n.t: Vagus nerve (X) and sympathetic fibres from the coeliac plexus.

a.t: Cystic artery, usually a branch of the right hepatic artery. The model does not draw it separately.

v.t: Cystic vein drains to the hepatic portal system.

n.t: Pelvic splanchnic (parasympathetic, S2-S4) and hypogastric (sympathetic) nerves.

a.t: Superior and inferior vesical arteries from the internal iliac artery.

v.t: Vesical venous plexus drains to the internal iliac vein.

n.t: Testicular plexus of sympathetic fibres from the aorticorenal region, with the genital branch of the genitofemoral nerve.

a.t: Left and right testicular arteries from the abdominal aorta. The model draws only the right one on its right side, so it is not highlighted.

v.t: Pampiniform plexus, which drains to the left and right testicular veins.

n.t: Parasympathetic secretomotor fibres from the glossopharyngeal nerve (IX) through the auriculotemporal nerve.

a.t: Maxillary artery and superficial temporal branches.

v.t: Retromandibular vein.

n.t: Parasympathetic fibres from the facial nerve (VII) through the chorda tympani, which joins the lingual nerve.

a.t: Facial artery and submental artery.

v.t: Facial vein.

n.t: Hypoglossal nerve (XII) for the muscles; lingual nerve and chorda tympani for sensation and taste.

a.t: Lingual artery from the external carotid. The model does not draw it separately.

v.t: Lingual veins drain to the internal jugular vein.
